main_body: Loom frame seen straight on: a brown outer frame with a top beam, a woven panel of white warp threads over a red and yellow checker band, a bottom beam, and two legs below.
top_band: Rows 10-13: orange beam with a tan band beneath it. The beam reads as a vertical front face, and the bottom beam at rows 22-25 repeats it symmetrically. No distinct horizontal surface is seen from above.
evidence: The top and bottom beams are mirror-image bands of the same orange and tan tones. Neither shows a lighter foreshortened top surface, a front-edge line, or an eave shadow. The warp threads and checker band are painted flat on a vertical plane. The legs are plain vertical posts. Compared with the reference stall and well, whose roofs and rims read as lighter horizontal bands, this is a front elevation.

style.evidence: The dark brown outline is tinted to match the wood, which is good. The beams have only about 3 tones (orange, tan, dark brown). The white and grey warp stripes and the red and yellow checker add some pattern. The brown side posts and the beam faces are flat fills with little grain, and the legs are plain 2-3 tone strips. Overall it is thinner than the richly shaded stall and well references.
